cells.tense: You are still carrying what you chose, and you know you are the one carrying it.
cells.ask: Offer one thing you keep, knowing it may come back changed. Holding without forcing — that is what lets what you carry stay alive in other hands.
cells.core: You are still carrying what you chose, and you know you are the one carrying it. The choosing happened long ago; what remains is steady and quiet. You bring what matters into how people speak and gather — not by pushing it at them, but by living it where they can see. That is what a living tradition looks like: someone who keeps showing up, and the thing stays warm because they do.\n\nWhat you carry has already proven it can hold. The work now is not to carry harder. Keep carrying as you have, and let what is already growing keep growing past you. Offer one thing you keep, and let it come back changed.
cells.sheetLine: You carry what you chose into the life people share. It holds, and it holds without pushing.
cells.verb: still following what you chose after everything that has happened
cells.place: in the customs and stories people hand to each other

cells.tense: You are braced for the moment the thing you keep will fall apart, and you are already living past it.
cells.ask: Let one thing stand without checking whether it still holds. Holding without forcing — that is what keeps what you carry alive instead of pushed to the edge of breaking.
cells.core: You are braced for the moment the thing you keep will fall apart, and you are already living past it. You reach ahead of the moment, testing whether what you carry still holds, whether anyone still wants it, whether the ending is already here. The reaching wears you down more than the carrying ever did.\n\nWhat you carry is still standing, but you cannot feel that because you are already past it. Stay with what is in front of you. Let one thing stand without checking it, and what you have built will show you it is stronger than your worry about it.
cells.sheetLine: You keep testing what is still standing, as if testing could prove whether the end will hold.
cells.verb: still following what you chose after everything that has happened
cells.place: in the customs and stories people hand to each other

cells.tense: You used to carry what mattered, and you are still standing where you stopped.
cells.ask: Tend one small thing you let go quiet, and let it grow at its own pace. Growing without forcing — that is what puts your hand back into the work you set down.
cells.core: You used to carry what mattered, and you are still standing where you stopped. The stories and practices you once kept alive went quiet in your hands, and you have not stepped back into the room where they live. The quiet is real. But it is not the end of the thread.\n\nWhat you knew how to keep going is still there. Go and tend one thing you let rest — a tradition, a gathering, a habit of speaking — without needing it to go well. Care that does not exhaust will pull you back into the work. The door is behind you; the work is in front.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped, and the work you once kept going is still waiting for your hand.
cells.verb: still following what you chose after everything that has happened
cells.place: in the customs and stories people hand to each other

cells.tense: You are already keeping the old things alive, and you speak as if they kept themselves.
cells.ask: Name one tradition you are keeping going and claim it as yours. The quiet holding you do is already enough — putting your name on it puts the pen back in your hand.
cells.core: You are already keeping the old things alive, and you speak as if they kept themselves. Something — the way you hold a gathering, the way you repeat a story, the way you show up — is doing the work of keeping meaning shared. You talk about these things as if they carry themselves, but what keeps them going is you, quietly, every time.\n\nYou are the one holding it. Say so about one thing you have been doing. It is not a boast. It is the plain fact that what you carry has your hands on it, and the whole life of it depends on your saying so.
cells.sheetLine: You keep it going. You just have not said that it is yours to keep going.
cells.verb: still following what you chose after everything that has happened
